svg.title: The IPC-4761 via treatments, in cross-section
svg.desc: Cross-sections of a 0.3 mm plated via in a 1.6 mm board, as a fab builds it: the plating lines the hole and joins the surface pads and two inner-layer pads; solder mask lies on the board surface. Open: mask pulled back, pads and hole exposed. Ia: mask laid over the pad and across the hole on one side only. Ib: the same on both sides. II: tented on both sides and covered with a second coat of mask. III: plugged a third of the way in from each side, air in the middle, pads exposed. IV: plugged, then covered with mask on both sides. V: completely filled, flush with the pads. VI: filled and covered with mask. VII: filled, then plated flat with copper over the hole, so a pad can sit on top. Ia is marked avoid: tenting one side only traps air and process chemistry. Type II is rarely used. Solder mask is a liquid coat that flows before it sets: thickest on bare FR4, thinnest at the copper's corners, and sagging where it spans a hole. Below, enlarged to true scale, the top of one via tented (left) and with the mask pulled back (right).

g.text: Enlarged, true scale: mask pulled back
Joins the surface and inner-layer pads
Solder mask over the pad and hole (the tent)
Copper cap, plated flat over the fill
The liquid levels out between features
A tent is thin and can crack
Rounded edge where the mask is pulled back
A 0.3 mm via in a 1.6 mm board, to scale. Copper and mask are drawn thicker than true scale so they show.
Enlarged views: copper about 50 µm with its plating, and mask about 25 µm on FR4 (an example; fabs vary).
"Tented" here means IPC's Type I, mask over ring and hole. Type II is rarely used.
